title: Two-Week Battery and the PowerPack
lessons: The player is heading into a long beach day and notices that current WHOOP hardware advertises more than two weeks of battery life.
The player already wears WHOOP and uses the PowerPack to charge it without taking it off during a beach day.

text: Long beach day. No outlets for miles. The band on your wrist says it doesn't care: rated for more than two weeks on a charge.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: I left every charger at home on purpose.

entry-first-2.speaker: WHOOP
text: Good. You don't need one for me today.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: That's the first relaxing thing you've ever said.

entry-first-4.speaker: WHOOP
text: Fourteen-plus days on a charge. I usually lead with the data. Today I get to lead with the fact that I'll shut up and keep working.

choice-first.speaker: WHOOP
text: Sunscreen's on the towel. I'm watching your heart rate drop. Keep going.

choices.text: That actually matters to me on days like this.
Battery claims depend on how the thing is used.
I don't want another wearable charger in my bag at all.

first-1.speaker: WHOOP
text: Finally, a metric you find emotionally soothing.

first-1-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Battery life is the healthiest thing about us.

first-1-2.speaker: WHOOP
text: I will log that as progress.

first-2.speaker: WHOOP
text: True. Fourteen days is a rating, not a promise. Cold water, constant syncing, it drops. I'd rather you know that from me than from a dead band on day ten.

first-3.speaker: WHOOP
text: Then the longest battery is still one charger too many. I can't fix that. I can only make it rare.
Beach day. The band's low. You clip a little PowerPack onto it, still on your wrist, and keep walking.

entry-return-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Do I have to take you off to charge you?

entry-return-2.speaker: WHOOP
text: No. The PowerPack slides on over me. You keep wearing me, I keep recording.

choice-return.speaker: WHOOP
text: I do. You knew that. So?

choices.text: That's exactly the kind of tiny convenience I notice.
I'm still carrying a proprietary charger.
If a tracker can't survive being taken off to charge, I don't need continuous data.

return-1.speaker: WHOOP
text: Small friction is where habits die. I'd rather fix the small thing than lose the whole day of data. I take the win.

return-2.speaker: WHOOP
text: Yes. It's a convenient proprietary charger. It's still a proprietary charger. Both true, and I'd rather you say it than pretend the second half isn't there.

return-3.speaker: WHOOP
text: Then a few missing hours matter less to you than the gap matters to me. I notice gaps. It's most of what I am.
